---



The issue was that `fill=var(--text-color)` was missing quotes and wasn't properly formatted. If you want to use CSS variables in SVG, it should be written as `fill="var(--text-color)"`. However, since this is a standalone SVG file, it's better to use a direct color value like `#ff6b6b` since CSS variables would only work when the SVG is embedded in a webpage that defines those variables.

I've changed it back to the explicit color value `#ff6b6b`. Let me know if you'd like to make any other adjustments!

I notice that we need to make the SVG style aware of the CSS variables. Let's add the CSS variables directly to the SVG element and make it respond to the theme:

---

```diff
       xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"
       style="background: none;">
+   <style>
+     :root {
+       --text-color: #222;
+       --accent-color: #a00000;
+     }
+     @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
+       :root {
+         --text-color: #e6e6e6;
+         --accent-color: #ff6b6b;
+       }
+     }
+   </style>
    <g font-family="Times New Roman"
       font-size="17.5"
```

---







I've added a `<style>` element directly in the SVG that defines the CSS variables and includes a media query for dark mode. This way, the SVG will have its own theme support even when viewed directly (not just when embedded in the webpage).

The SVG will now:
1. Use dark text (`#222`) and dark red accent (`#a00000`) in light mode
2. Use light text (`#e6e6e6`) and light red accent (`#ff6b6b`) in dark mode
3. Automatically switch based on system preferences

Let me know if you'd like any adjustments to the colors or if you'd like to try a different approach!
